Run a local database OAuth demo

Source: R/demo.R
oauth_db_demo.Rd

Start a database and Keycloak sign-in using Docker, with a small Shiny app running either in Docker or in a local R process. The installed package includes the configuration, accounts and sample data; no source checkout or cloud account is needed.

Usage

oauth_db_demo(
  database = c("postgres", "postgrest", "trino", "starrocks", "duckdb", "libsql",
    "cratedb", "opensearch"),
  action = c("start", "stop", "files", "services"),
  path = NULL,
  launch_browser = interactive(),
  build = TRUE,
  app = c("docker", "local")
)

Arguments

database

Demo to run: "postgres" (the default), "postgrest", "trino", "starrocks", "duckdb" (Quack), "libsql", "cratedb", or "opensearch".

action

"start" runs the demo until you stop it or interrupt R. "stop" removes its containers and data, including after a forced exit. "files" copies the configuration without starting Docker. "services" starts only the Docker services and returns settings for an app you run in the current R session; app is ignored in this mode.

path

Directory for the demo files. Defaults to a database-specific directory in R's user cache. Existing demo files are kept so you can edit the app or configuration. An unrelated nonempty directory is refused.

launch_browser

Open the app in your browser once it is ready. Services-only mode leaves browser launch to your app.

build

Build Docker images before starting. Set to FALSE to reuse images from a previous successful build.

app

Where to run the Shiny app: "docker" (the default) supplies its R environment and drivers, or "local" uses your installed R packages. Local mode creates an editable app under local-app/<database>/ in path.

Value

Invisibly, the directory containing the demo configuration. With action = "services", an environment containing provider (a configured shinyOAuth provider), url (the local data endpoint), host, port, ca_bundle (for HTTPS endpoints), path and a stop() function instead.

Details

Install and start Docker with Linux containers and Docker Compose v2. The first build downloads images, R packages and pinned package sources from GitHub. PostgreSQL also compiles its native OAuth runtime. Allow several minutes and a few GB of disk space. StarRocks uses amd64 images and needs about 4 GB of Docker memory; other architectures need emulation. DuckDB installs a matching R client and Quack extensions; the client compiles from source if a Linux binary isn't available. OpenSearch needs about 2 GB of Docker memory for its database container.

Open http://localhost:18100 and sign in as alice with password alice, or bob with password bob. Keycloak uses a generated test certificate at https://localhost:18443; your browser may ask you to accept it for this local demo.

Run one demo at a time: they share the same loopback ports. All accounts are public demo accounts. Containers bind browser ports to loopback only. Clicking Stop demo, or interrupting the foreground R call, removes the demo's containers and volumes. The copied files and cached images stay. A separate R session can use action = "stop" after a forced exit.

To edit an example, first use action = "files", edit the returned directory, then call with the same path. app.R in the selected database's subdirectory is the Shiny app. Stop the demo before rebuilding.

Run and edit the app locally

Use app = "local" to keep the database and sign-in services in Docker while running Shiny in a separate R process on your computer. This uses your R library and watches the copied local-app/<database>/app.R for changes. Save the file and reload the browser to try your edits. Existing app files are preserved. Local and Docker modes have separate default cache directories.

Local mode requires callr and bslib 0.9.0 or later. Trino also needs RTrino; StarRocks needs odbc and MySQL Connector/ODBC with its OpenID Connect plugin; DuckDB needs a client matching the demo server (DuckDB 1.5.4) and installs its matching Quack/httpfs extensions. PostgreSQL's native client requires Linux and shinyOAuthDB/RPostgres built against the same shared libpq 18. Use the PostgREST demo for local editing on Windows or macOS without a database driver.

The launcher copies the demo's public CA certificate and trusts it only inside the local app process. It does not change your certificate store or the parent R session's TLS settings. Local mode requires Compose 2.24.4 or later and publishes its database endpoint on loopback port 19444.

Run your own app with Docker services

Use action = "services" to start the database and sign-in infrastructure without starting Shiny or blocking R. Use the returned provider in shinyOAuth::oauth_client() and url in an API helper. This mode needs Compose 2.24.4 or later but does not install or require local database drivers. Native database clients still need their usual runtime; PostgREST works in local R on Windows, macOS and Linux.

Browser sign-in uses HTTPS. The returned provider uses Keycloak's HTTP endpoints on loopback port 18080 for R's token, UserInfo and signing-key requests. It retains the HTTPS issuer and validates signed ID tokens. This avoids changing R's certificate store or curl settings. PostgREST's services-only endpoint uses HTTP on 127.0.0.1:19444, permitted only while its demo handle is active. Other data endpoints retain HTTPS and supply ca_bundle for clients that support custom certificate authorities.

During this demo, shinyOAuth's host policy permits loopback hosts and its loopback-only OIDC development option is enabled. demo$stop() removes the containers and data and restores these options. Register it with shiny::onStop() when your app starts. Services are also stopped when the returned object is garbage collected or R exits. Run one demo at a time, and stop it before starting another. Using action = "stop" with the same database and path also retires any services handle in the current R process and restores its options.

See also

oauth_db_postgres(), oauth_db_postgrest_api(), oauth_db_trino(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_duckdb(), oauth_db_libsql_api(), oauth_db_cratedb_api(), oauth_db_opensearch_api().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
oauth_db_demo()
oauth_db_demo("postgrest")
oauth_db_demo("trino")
oauth_db_demo("starrocks")
oauth_db_demo("duckdb")
oauth_db_demo("libsql")
oauth_db_demo("cratedb")
oauth_db_demo("opensearch")
oauth_db_demo(action = "stop")
path <- oauth_db_demo(action = "files")
# Edit a local R app backed by PostgreSQL and PostgREST in Docker:
path <- oauth_db_demo("postgrest", app = "local", action = "files")
file.edit(file.path(path, "local-app", "postgrest", "app.R"))
oauth_db_demo("postgrest", app = "local", path = path)
# Run your own app against PostgreSQL through PostgREST:
demo <- oauth_db_demo("postgrest", action = "services")
demo$provider
demo$url
demo$stop()
} # }
